## 1. The good word and the evil word as trees  (`#the-two-trees`)

Cited ayat: 14:24-27

> **14:24** أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا كَلِمَةً طَيِّبَةً كَشَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ أَصْلُهَا ثَابِتٌ وَفَرْعُهَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
>
> **14:25** تُؤْتِىٓ أُكُلَهَا كُلَّ حِينٍۭ بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهَا وَيَضْرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ
>
> **14:26** وَمَثَلُ كَلِمَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ كَشَجَرَةٍ خَبِيثَةٍ ٱجْتُثَّتْ مِن فَوْقِ ٱلْأَرْضِ مَا لَهَا مِن قَرَارٍ
>
> **14:27** يُثَبِّتُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِٱلْقَوْلِ ٱلثَّابِتِ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَفِى ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ وَيُضِلُّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ وَيَفْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ مَا يَشَآءُ

### Claims

**c1** (14:24): The ayah asks whether one has seen how God struck a similitude: a good word is like a good tree, its root firm and its branch in the sky.

**c2** (14:25): The tree gives its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord, and God strikes similitudes for people that they may remember.

**c3** (14:26): The similitude of an evil word is like an evil tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, with no steadiness.

**c4** (14:27): God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter, and He leaves the wrongdoers astray, and God does what He wills.

### One-minute summary

The ayat give a similitude of a good word as a good tree with a firm root and a branch in the sky, and of an evil word as an evil tree uprooted from the surface of the earth [c1][c3]. They add that God makes firm those who believe with the firm word [c4].

### Complete story

The ayah asks whether one has seen how God struck a similitude: a good word is like a good tree, its root firm and its branch in the sky [c1]. The tree gives its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord [c2]. God strikes similitudes for people that they may remember [c2].

The similitude of an evil word is like an evil tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, with no steadiness [c3]. God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the hereafter [c4]. He leaves the wrongdoers astray, and God does what He wills [c4].

### Deep study

The ayat pair a good word and an evil word with a good tree and an evil tree, the one firm and the other uprooted [c1][c3]. The good tree has a firm root and gives fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord [c1][c2]. The closing ayah turns from the trees to people and speaks of the firm word [c4].

### Kids mode

A good word is like a good tree with a firm root and a branch in the sky [c1]. It gives fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord [c2]. An evil word is like an evil tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, with no steadiness [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat set a good word beside an evil word through the picture of a good tree and an evil tree [c1][c3]. Another reading is that the closing ayah speaks of God making firm those who believe with the firm word [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which good word or which evil word is meant; the ayat name neither, and they do not name the kind of tree.
- Not established: what the firm word in 14:27 is; the ayah does not define it.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later commentary identifies the good word, the evil word and the firm word with particular sayings and with particular moments; this draft does not repeat or vouch for them.
- The ayah itself says that God struck a similitude (mathal).
